newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hysan says HK office market stabilises.
newsitem.headline: Hysan says HK office market stabilises.

text.p: Hysan Development Ltd said on Tuesday the top-of-the-line Hong Kong office rental market had reached bottom and the company expected a recovery in rentals.
Hysan said the Grade A office rental market appeared to be either at the bottom, or close to the bottom of the cycle.
"Prospective tenants of Grade A office space...should anticipate a gradual hardening of rental levels," Pauline Wong, Hysan's director of property said.
Hysan said recent research showed a major slowdown in the decline of rentals in the second quarter of 1996.

The decline on Hong Kong Island slowed to 0.74 percent in Central and 0.93 percent in Causeway Bay and Wanchai, down from 1.60 and 2.38 percent in the first quarter and 8.84 and 6.77 percent in the last quarter of 1995, Hysan noted.
The research showed the 1.6 million square feet of new Grade A office space available in Hong Kong this year was insufficient to meet the demand expected, it said.
Hysan said demand from mainland Chinese companies and from multinationals could rise substantially with a buoyant Chinese economy.
The company is redeveloping Hong Kong's old Lee Gardens Hotel in downtown Causeway Bay into an office and retail complex, scheduled for completion in the first quarter of 1997.
Wong said Hysan was finalising deals with close to half of the office space in Lee Gardens.
In September Hysan reported profit attributable to shareholders of HK$697.45 million for the first six months in 1996, a 10.31 percent rise over the equivalent period of 1995.
